Keywords: Development of a highly efficient trifunctional electrocatalyst for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), oxygen
Trifunctional electrocatalyst evolution reaction (OER) and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is essential in a variety of energy conversion
Acidic conditions technologies, such as H2-O2 fuel cell and overall water splitting. However, state-of-the-art electrocatalysts (Pt, Ir,
Water splitting
Ru) for these electrochemical reactions suffer from high cost. Therefore, search for novel and cost-effective
H2-O2 fuel cell
Density functional theory
metal-based catalysts have gained tremendous attention. In this work, we investigated a novel Cd based elec­
trocatalysts as efficient trifunctional electrocatalysts by density functional theory analysis. An in-depth reaction
mechanism of CdN4C0-gra and CdN0C4-gra structure in acidic conditions had been investigated. After a detailed
and systematic analysis by partial densities of states (PDOS) and Gibbs free energy (ΔG) of various modeled
catalytic systems, the catalysts system composed of CdN4C0-gra showed excellent electrocatalytic properties with
an overpotential of (ƞHER = 0.05 V, ƞOER = 0.48 V, and ƞORR = 0.75 V).

3.3. Reaction mechanism of ORR, OER and HER in CdN4C0-gra and
CdN0C4-gra systems

ORR and OER are all four electronic steps, as shown in eq. (6)–(9).
ORR is exothermic reaction and OER is endothermic reaction. Therefore,
the reaction step with the least heat release is the rate determining step
of ORR, on the contrary, the reaction step with the most heat absorption
is the rate determining step of OER. The reaction can be divided into four
routes, and the reaction pathways of OER and ORR affected by H2O on
Cd–N–C-doped graphene system is shown in Fig. 6, the others are shown
in Fig. S4. The substrate under the action of two water molecules be­
comes after the first step reaction removes a hydrogen atom OH* with
one water molecule. In another case, after adsorbing a water molecule,
the substrate loses a hydrogen atom and finally becomes a structure of
OH*. Both generated structures may become O* or 2OH*, and then all
